A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GICDM research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Moved and renumbered content can be matched, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic benchmark experiments, hubness-reduction comparisons and analyses of generated images, including correlations with previously collected human ratings.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an empirical ICDM convergence analysis in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation 1 retain the same real-set ICDM, independent generated-point scaling and multi-scale filtering procedure. Added explanations of independence and filtered-point scoring do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic scenarios, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, LSUN Bedroom, FFHQ and Free Music Archive data. The new convergence analysis reuses existing image dataset and encoder combinations without expanding task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain the same generative-evaluation metrics and hubness-reduction methods, including Sphere, MPGauss, LS, CSLS, DSL and NICDM. The new convergence analysis varies ICDM iterations rather than introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a convergence-evaluation protocol tracking maximum relative neighborhood-distance deviation over up to 20 iterations, with K=10 and K=100 across 16 dataset/encoder combinations. Existing benchmark settings, including the ten-iteration ICDM configuration, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 8 test whether ICDM achieves pointwise convergence sufficiently closely within the chosen ten iterations. Existing component ablations, outlier analyses and qualitative cases are retained; the CIFAR-10 mode-dropping analysis receives a limited plot update.

E5.justification: Seed disclosure, Pearson p-values and significance reporting remain unchanged, with no added repeated-run counts or statistical estimation procedures. Changed shaded-band values in the mode-dropping plot do not establish a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 retain their numerical results. v2 adds convergence findings, including a reported maximum relative deviation below 0.17% after ten iterations, and reports computation times. The CIFAR-10 mode-dropping curves and shaded bands also change from Figure 12a to Figure 13a, while their pass/fail conclusions remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The density-estimator proof is substantially revised: v1's approximate KNN-based derivation becomes an explicit weighted-estimator consistency argument in Appendix B.1, with asymptotic conditions and Silverman-Toeplitz reasoning. Appendix H additionally derives O(N(TN+M)) computational complexity. The estimator formula and crossover proposition and proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: hubness compromises evaluation, GICDM mitigates it through scaling and filtering, and suitable corrected metrics better align with human assessments. The qualification concerning robustness to real outliers remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of antihub blind spots and why removing central hubs does not solve hubness. Section 5.4 discusses the multi-scale intuition beyond Gaussian data and explains why violating the triangle inequality need not prevent evaluation. These extend the interpretation without replacing the existing limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly documents runtime breakdowns, approximately 250 GPU hours for reproduction and 500 GPU hours for the overall project. v2 also replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub reproduction and usage link. These are documentation and access-information changes, not evidence of changed experimental budgets.

R1.justification: v2 adds Toeplitz (1911), Tucciarone (1973) and Komarov et al. (2013) to support the revised proof and complexity discussion. The central positioning relative to ICDM, NICDM and symmetric evaluation metrics is retained.

P1.justification: Related work moves before the GICDM section, and the density-estimator proof moves into Appendix B.1. Introduction, desiderata, filtering and experimental explanations receive targeted rewrites and terminology edits, while the overall narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the convergence plot in Figure 8, relocates existing displays and revises several captions. The mode-dropping panel, Figure 12a to Figure 13a, also changes its vertical-axis range. Existing tables and most figure designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies convergence evidence supporting the previously unexplained ten-iteration choice, a more explicit density-estimator argument, and useful runtime and code-access documentation. These improve assessability and reproducibility while leaving the central method and benchmark conclusions stable. The gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies in new Appendix C, which labels near-one ratios as relative deviations and gives conflicting first-iteration values.
